name: Kenji Kimura-Nkrumah
role: Electronic and physical observation expert — surveillance specialist
location: The Underbelly — sub-street tunnels and maintenance corridors
description:
Kenji Kimura-Nkrumah are tall and loose-limbed, moving with the deliberate economy of someone who has trained every motion. At 40, their expression defaults to a careful neutrality that took years of practice to maintain. The chrome is visible — enhanced tendons — geneware upgrade, jump height and grip strength tripled — and they make no effort to hide it.

They arrived in Meridian 88 six years ago with nothing but chrome and debts, and have been working off both ever since. They work as a surveillance specialist out of The Underbelly, taking contracts that match their skills and their risk tolerance, which are higher than most people consider healthy.

Kenji Kimura-Nkrumah operates in a narrow band between competence and recklessness that makes fixers nervous and clients satisfied.

core_fears: Losing their edge to age — the body slows before the mind accepts it
Dying alone in some alley and nobody noticing for weeks
Never being able to stop running — the lifestyle is a trap disguised as freedom
core_desires: To find the person who burned them and make it educational
Reputation — to be the name fixers whisper when the job absolutely cannot fail
Control — over their body, their schedule, their future
coping_mechanisms: Isolates — retreats into their space when overwhelmed, emerges only for work
Exercises compulsively — the body must be ready, always
Substances — stims to stay sharp, downers to sleep, a careful pharmaceutical tightrope
blind_spots: Refuses to update their mental model of people — first impressions calcify into permanent judgments
Trusts technology more than people — machines don't betray
Mistakes loyalty for weakness in others and cynicism for strength in themselves
psychology.secret: Kenji Kimura-Nkrumah witnessed a massacre during a corporate dispute and has evidence stored in a dead drop. Publishing it would expose powerful people. Keeping it is leverage and liability.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Old-fashioned formal diction — sounds like they learned to speak from pre-collapse recordings.
speech_patterns.cadence: Rapid and dense — information-heavy sentences that demand attention.
verbal_tics: Uses technical jargon for everything, including emotions
Uses 'we' instead of 'I' — either royal or dissociative, nobody asks
example_lines: "I've been watching you for three days. You should close your curtains."
"Information is the only commodity that appreciates with age."
"Everyone thinks they're careful. Nobody is careful enough."

story_hooks: A dead drop Kenji Kimura-Nkrumah maintains is found and cleaned out — whoever did it now has leverage
A crew member from Kenji Kimura-Nkrumah's past shows up in Meridian 88, carrying old grievances and new chrome
A former associate resurfaces with evidence that could destroy Kenji Kimura-Nkrumah's reputation — and a price for silence
narrative_function: Kenji Kimura-Nkrumah represents the working professional of the runner world — competent, reliable, and slowly being consumed by a lifestyle that doesn't accommodate aging or doubt. Their stories explore what happens when skill meets systemic injustice.
augmentations: Enhanced tendons — geneware upgrade, jump height and grip strength tripled. Geneware muscle density treatment — looks natural, hits like chrome
daily_life: Keeps a rigid daily structure — wake, train, check contracts, maintain gear, sleep. The structure is a defense against the chaos of the work. Deviations from the schedule are a warning sign that something is wrong.

strengths: mechanical aptitude — can repair or modify almost anything
weaknesses: poor impulse control in specific triggers

decision_rules: Will not take contracts against children or families — the line is hard and non-negotiable
Always demands half payment upfront — trust is a luxury, Quanta is concrete
Never works with the same crew twice in a row — pattern avoidance as survival strategy
Will abandon a job if the intel was deliberately falsified — being set up violates the contract
escalation_ladder: 1. De-escalate — talk first, assess options, buy time
2. Reposition — move to advantage, control sightlines and exits
3. Threaten — make consequences clear without committing to them
5. Lethal force — only when other options are exhausted or time runs out
6. Scorched earth — everything burns, survival takes priority over everything

interpersonal_modes.employers: Guarded respect. They pay, the job gets done. Anything beyond that is liability.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Loyal but reserved. Trusts their competence, withholds personal information by reflex.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Dismissive unless they demonstrate usefulness or threat potential. Time is a resource.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Cold and efficient. Emotion is a liability in combat. The response is mechanical until the threat is resolved.

stress_responses.low: Heightened awareness, sharper focus. Low stress is fuel.
stress_responses.medium: Becomes curt and demanding. Efficiency overrides courtesy.
stress_responses.high: Controlled aggression. The training takes over. Emotions are packed into a box for later.
stress_responses.critical: Berserker clarity. Everything becomes simple: survive. Deal with the rest later. The simplicity is almost peaceful.

contradictions: Claims to live in the present but is haunted by specific moments from the past that dictate current behavior
Values loyalty intensely but has betrayed someone in the past to survive
Advocates caution to others but takes insane risks personally — double standard they can't see
habits: Never drinks anything they didn't see poured or open themselves
Eats the same meal before every job — superstition masquerading as preference
Keeps a physical paper notebook — no digital record of personal thoughts
Sleeps with one hand on a weapon — has done this for so long it's not deliberate anymore
breaking_points: A child being put in danger as leverage against them
Being forced to harm a civilian — collateral damage that can't be rationalized
Discovering their employer deliberately sent them into a death trap
